title: Thyroid scan
what: A small dose of a tracer substance is injected into a vein. The thyroid takes it up, and a camera shows which areas are more active.
why: For an overactive thyroid, to find the cause, or for thyroid nodules, to see which are active.
duration: the whole visit usually takes 1 to 2 hours; the report in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you are breastfeeding. You will need a break
If in the last 1 to 2 months you had a CT with contrast or took iodine

prepare.title: Iodine
prepare.text: Iodine supplements are usually stopped a few weeks before the test. Ask the clinic how long.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Thyroid medicines are sometimes paused. Do not do this on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off necklaces and jewelry from your neck.

steps: You get an injection into a vein
You lie on your back with your head tilted back a little
The camera is placed over your neck. Keep still and try not to swallow
The scan takes a few minutes
feel: The injection feels like giving blood
You do not feel the tracer at all
after: You can go on with your normal day
Drink water and use the toilet more often
Ask the clinic about breastfeeding and contact with babies
Take the report to an endocrinologist

faq.q: Why no iodine before the test?
faq.a: Iodine fills up the thyroid, so the tracer is not taken up well. The scan will not be accurate.
No. Ultrasound shows the structure, and the scan shows how the gland works. They are often done together.

reminders.text: Thyroid scan tomorrow. Bring your hormone tests and thyroid ultrasound.
